chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Sukayn ibn Ammar, from a man from our companions who was teknonymed Abu Ahmad, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during the Tawaf, his hand in my hand, when a man presented himself to me having a need for me. So I gestured to him with my hand and said to him, 'Stay as you are until I finish my Tawaf.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, 'What is this?' I said, 'May Allah keep you well, a man came to me regarding a need.' He said to me, 'Is he a Muslim?' I said, 'Yes.'

So he said to me, 'Go with him regarding his need.' I said to him, 'May Allah keep you well, should I cut the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And even if I was in the Obligatory one?' He said, 'Yes, and even if you were in the Obligatory one.'

He said, 'And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever walks with his Muslim brother regarding his need, Allah will write for him a thousand thousand good deeds, erase from him a thousand thousand sins, and raise for him a thousand thousand levels.'
ai.seo_question: Should one interrupt obligatory Tawaf to help a Muslim brother with a need?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of prioritizing social obligations (fard al-ayn or fard al-kifaya) over individual acts of worship, establishing that assisting a brother in need supersedes the continuity of Tawaf, even in its obligatory form. The immense reward of a thousand thousand good deeds underscores the spiritual weight of social solidarity, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on 'Huquq al-Nas' (Rights of People) as a core component of piety.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Sukeyn Bin Ammar, from a man from our companions teknonymed as Abu Ahmad, who said,

‘I was with Abu Abdullahasws in the Tawaaf, hisasws hand being in my hand, when a man presented himself to me having a need for him to me. So, I gestured to him with my hand saying, ‘Stay where you are until I am free from my Tawaaf’. So Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘Who is this?’ I said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! A man who came to me regarding a need’. So heasws said to me: ‘Is he a Muslim?’ I said, ‘Yes’.

So heasws said to me: ‘Go with him regarding his need’. So I said to himasws, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! So I should cut the Tawaaf?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘And even if I was in the Obligatory one?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, and even if you were in the Obligatory one’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who walks along with his Muslim brother with regards to his need, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him a thousand thousand good deeds, and Delete from him a thousand thousand sins, and Rasie for him a thousand thousand Levels’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il ibn Bazi’ from ‘Isma‘il ibn al-Sarraj from Sukayn ibn ‘Ammar from a man from our called Abu Ahmad who has said the following:

“I was performing Tawaf with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, with his hand in my hand that a man came by who needed me for something. I made a gesture to him with my hand to indicate that he should wait until I complete my Tawaf. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘Who is he?’ I replied, ‘May Allah keep you well, he is a man who needs me for something.’ He (the Imam) then asked, ‘Is he a Muslim?’ I replied, ‘Yes, he is.’

He (the Imam) then told me to go with him to help in his needs. I then said, ‘May Allah keep you well, can I leave my Tawaf for his needs?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Even if it is obligatory Tawaf?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, even if you are in an obligatory Tawaf.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Whoever walks for his Muslim brother in faith to help him in his needs, Allah writes for him one million good deeds and deletes one million of his sins and raises for him one million degree.’”
